FRENCH — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good night only
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Excuse me
   D. Thank you

2. When practising Interactive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Listening.

3. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.

4. When practising Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.

5. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

6. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.

7. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. porte
   B. chaise
   C. livre
   D. fenêtre

8. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.

9. When practising Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

10. When practising Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing Clarity Vocabulary Fluidity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing Vocabulary Handwriting Creativity Clarity and conciseness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
